findings.evidence: Full-time employees ... are eligible (Eligibility) / Employees must submit the receipt (How to Apply) / The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days (Approval Timeline) / The applicant must keep the equipment in good working condition (Restrictions and Exceptions) / You record the stipend item on the request form (Terminology Notes)
findings.fix: Pick one term for the person applying for the stipend and use it in every section, or add a one-line definition stating that employee, applicant, and requester all mean the same reader.
findings.location: Eligibility; How to Apply; Approval Timeline; Restrictions and Exceptions; Terminology Notes
findings.violation: Five different terms (employee, staff, requester, applicant, you) are used interchangeably across sections for the single person applying for and receiving the stipend, with no stated equivalence, so a reader cannot be sure a rule stated for the applicant also binds the employee or the requester.

findings.evidence: the benefits team tracks the stipend budget (Program Overview) / eligibility for the workspace stipend depends on several details (Eligibility) / the home-office equipment stipend (Eligibility, paragraph 1) / You record the stipend item on the request form (Terminology Notes)
findings.fix: Use one name for the benefit throughout, or state explicitly that workspace stipend and stipend item both refer to the home-office equipment stipend.
findings.violation: The benefit is named four different ways (the stipend, the home-office equipment stipend, the workspace stipend, the stipend item) with nothing in the document stating whether these are the same benefit or different ones, so a reader cannot tell whether the workspace-location rules in Eligibility paragraph 3 apply to the same stipend the rest of the document describes.

findings.evidence: Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt.
findings.fix: Move Request Steps immediately after Eligibility and before Approval Timeline, so the reader meets the starting steps before the sections that assume the request is already underway.
findings.location: Request Steps (after Approval Timeline, Required Documentation, Reimbursement Amounts, Restrictions and Exceptions, Terminology Notes)
findings.violation: The section naming the actual first steps of the process (confirm eligibility, upload receipt) appears after four sections that only make sense once a request already exists (how long approval takes, what documentation to keep, how reimbursement is evaluated, and restrictions), so a reader trying to start the process has to read past all of that first.

findings.evidence: Special Cases: The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time. / Questions and Updates: The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. / Terminology Notes: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month.
findings.fix: Either fill these three sections with the content their headings promise (actual exception handling, an actual contact or update channel, and actual term definitions) or remove the headings and fold the repeated budget-tracking sentence into Program Overview once.
findings.location: Special Cases; Questions and Updates; Terminology Notes
findings.violation: A reader scanning headings for help with an edge case, a place to ask a question, or a definition of a term finds none of that: Special Cases and Questions and Updates both just repeat the fiscal-year budget-tracking statement from Program Overview nearly verbatim, and Terminology Notes contains a reimbursement-processing sequence rather than any defined term, so the reader's search by heading fails even though the headings promise exactly that content.

findings.evidence: 71-word sentence, 5 subordinate-clause markers: Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category.
findings.fix: Split the sentence at a subordinate-clause boundary.
findings.violation: The sentence runs to 71 words with 5 subordinate-clause markers, longer than the reader can hold in mind on a single pass.

findings.evidence: The determination of stipend eligibility happens before any payment goes out. The escalation of repeat requests happens automatically within the same quarter. / Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt.
findings.fix: Name the actor as the sentence's subject: the manager determines eligibility before approving payment; the benefits team escalates a repeat request automatically within the same quarter; the employee begins the request by confirming eligibility and uploading the receipt.
findings.violation: Every sentence in Review Responsibility, and the opening of Request Steps, runs its action through an abstract noun (the determination, the escalation, completing the request) instead of naming who determines eligibility, who escalates repeat requests, or who completes the request, so a reader cannot tell who is actually responsible for any of it.

findings.evidence: 71-word sentence: Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category.
findings.fix: Move subordinate clauses and modifiers after the main clause, not between its subject and verb.
findings.violation: At 71 words, with 0 comma-set-off clause(s) and 5 subordinate-clause marker(s), the sentence stacks interruptions between its subject and its main verb instead of holding the main clause together.

findings.evidence: Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device because fieldwork regularly takes the employee away from the single fixed desk that the standard equipment list assumes every applicant has for the whole benefit year while the finance office tracks the second device against the same annual amount that the equipment catalog publishes for each category.
findings.fix: End the sentence on the fieldwork justification for a second device, and move the finance-office tracking detail to its own, later sentence.
findings.violation: The newest, most important element, that fieldwork can justify a second device, is buried in the middle of the sentence, and the sentence instead ends on the already-established fact that the finance office tracks spending against the catalog's annual amount, so the reader's attention lands on routine bookkeeping rather than on the exception that actually changes what the policy allows.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. The team logs each request the moment it arrives. / The determination of stipend eligibility happens before any payment goes out. The escalation of repeat requests happens automatically within the same quarter.
findings.fix: Label these sections as internal process notes, move them to an appendix, or rewrite them to tell the employee what to expect rather than describing the internal workflow.
findings.location: Program Coordination and Review Responsibility sections
findings.violation: These two sections describe internal benefits-team workflow (routing, logging, escalation) with no instruction the employee reader can act on, interleaved among sections written for the employee applicant (Eligibility, How to Apply, Required Documentation) without being marked as background or internal-only, so a reader cannot tell whether the section is for them.

findings.evidence: Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order before the review begins.
findings.fix: Reformat the inline items as a numbered or bulleted list.
findings.violation: The sentence embeds three or more comma- or semicolon-separated parallel items inline rather than presenting them as a formatted list.

findings.evidence: Additionally, employees shall retain receipts for one year after the purchase date.
findings.violation: The sentence states a binding requirement using shall or an indirect requirement phrasing instead of must.

findings.evidence: The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount.
findings.fix: Restate the nominalized noun as the sentence's main verb.
findings.violation: The action is buried inside the noun 'evaluation', carried by a generic support verb, instead of stated as the sentence's own main verb.

findings.fix: Split the paragraph so each part covers one topic.
findings.violation: The paragraph exceeds the 150-word scannability threshold.
